1Purpose

This policy is the frame for the module at [Provider name]. It names the seven standards we work to and the policy that carries each one, the roles that run the module, and the rules that apply across the whole module. It sets no time limit and restates no commitment of its own: each of POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 holds its commitments, its clocks and its checks in one place. It is for families, our workers, the other services in a 's team, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their , from first contact until supports end.
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children or families: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we work: the family home, early learning and school settings, community places, our premises, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy is the shared frame for the module. POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 each set out one standard in full, with its own commitments, times and checks; nothing in this policy changes them. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safety rules for all our work with children; until it is written, the appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule.

3Commitments

C1

We will do what POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the child, s 56).

C2

We will do what POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the family, s 57).

C3

We will do what POL-ECS-04 Inclusion Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (inclusion, s 58).

C4

We will do what POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (collaboration, s 59).

C5

We will do what POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (capacity building, s 60).

C6

We will do what POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (evidence-informed supports, s 61).

C7

We will do what POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (outcome based approach, s 62).

4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before everything else in this policy. A worker who is worried about a child acts on that worry first.

G2

A person with decides about the child's supports. We ask for the child's own views in a way that fits their age and how they communicate, and we record them.

G3

One route for every concern. A practice concern goes to the . A conduct or safety concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body, or in a sole trader's business to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A child who may be at goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). The person a concern is about never handles it.

G4

The time limits of the module are set in POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 and the procedures under them; the Module clocks table at the end of these ground rules reproduces them, and this policy sets none of its own. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

G5

The appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule: the law of [state or territory] on who must report, the test, where, how fast, and the duty of every adult to tell police of child sexual abuse. POL-CHS-01, when written, holds the wider child safe standards and reportable conduct rules. The Quality Manager checks the schedule every 12 months and when the law changes.

G6

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is the one register for the module and holds dates, names, counts and record numbers. The forms hold the detail and the family's words.

G7

A family can say no to a , a referral, a team meeting or a question. Saying no is recorded and is never a reason to reduce supports.

G8

A complaint made by a child or family at any point is handled under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. A child's "stop" or "not happy" signal is a complaint the child can make in their own way.

G9

A sole trader holds every role except practice supervisor and independent contact for concerns. An outside practice supervisor with early childhood experience and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register are the checks on the sole trader's own work.

G10

The is the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row. Where the family chooses a key worker from our team, the key worker is the plan lead, and when the key worker changes the plan-lead role moves with it the same day.

9Words we use

345 words
early childhood supports
supports for a young child with developmental delay or disability, and their family, under the registration class "early intervention supports for early childhood".
family
the parents, carers and other people who raise the child, as the family itself describes them.
parental responsibility
the legal authority to make decisions for a child. A court or child protection order can change who holds it.
support network
the relatives, friends, educators and others in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.
everyday routines
the things the child does most days, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed and going to early learning.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker, that person is the plan lead.
team around the child
the family, our practitioners and the other providers who work together on the child's plan.
plan lead
the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners.
practitioner drafting for the plan lead
the practitioner the plan lead asks to draft the plan under PRO-ECS-08. The plan lead stays accountable for the plan.
functional outcome
something the child will do in daily life, written so the family can see when it has happened.
coaching
helping a parent, carer or educator practise a strategy in their own routine, in place of doing it for them.
both clearances
an NDIS worker screening clearance, and the working with children check of [state or territory].
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.
risk of harm
the words this module uses for the reporting threshold. Our test is that you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. The appendix to POL-ECS-02 gives the exact term used in [state or territory].
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

A young often has several services in their life at once. This policy sets how [Provider name] works as one team with the and those services. The family never has to carry messages between them.

2Applies to

  • Every practitioner, and manager of ours who works with those children. This covers employees, contractors, students and volunteers.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every is supported in a family-centred way from their first day. Every practitioner starts from what the family knows and wants at every contact. A family that has a has one first call, who keeps the family's priorities in front of the team.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1, C3, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C12 and C13.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • a family accepts our offer of (steps 1 to 4)
  • any practitioner has a contact with the family: a session, a call, a message or a meeting (steps 5 to 13)
  • the family has chosen a key worker, has chosen none, or wants to change (steps 14 to 20)
  • the family says no, asks for a change, sees something differently, or is unhappy (steps 21 to 24 and Decision table 1)
  • a plan review is due (step 25).

Who acts:

  • The Service Manager names the and a backup.
  • The plan lead opens the 's row, explains how we work, and is the family's first call where the family chose no key worker.
  • The key worker is the one practitioner the family chose as their main contact. The key worker may be ours or from another service. Where the key worker is ours, they are the plan lead.
  • Every practitioner works the family-centred way at every contact.
  • The Quality Manager samples contact records every 3 months.

In a small provider the Service Manager and the plan lead are one person. A sole trader holds every role, and is the key worker if the family chooses them. A sole trader asks the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register to read a sample of 3 family records every 6 months.

3Before you start

  • The family has accepted our offer and the intake is done (FRM-SUP-01 Referral and Intake Form).
  • The family has a record, FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record, or will have one under PRO-ECS-03 The Family Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).
  • The offer of a key worker and the family's choice are made under PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). They are recorded in Section D of FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record. This procedure starts from that choice.
  • The child's safety controls line is agreed under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) step 2. The first session does not go ahead while column I of REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is empty for the type of setting it is in. That is the only pre-session gate.

4Watch out

  • Telling before asking makes the practitioner the only expert. The family's knowledge is lost, and the family stops speaking up. Ask first.
  • A strategy that does not fit the family's week will not be used. The family is blamed, and the child gets no benefit. Work inside their routines.
  • "Do you understand?" gets a yes whatever the truth. The family leaves unsure what to do. Ask them to say or show it back.
  • A family's no is a choice. Reducing a support because of a no punishes the child. It can breach the duty to respect self-determination and decision-making (Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(a)).
  • A child's safety comes before a family's choice. If you think a child may be at , tell the the same day. A delay can leave a child in danger.
  • A child or a brother or sister who interprets can change what is said. The meaning is lost, and a child carries an adult's worries.

5Steps

Start with a new family

Step 1

The Service Manager

Name the plan lead and a backup for the child.

Choose a practitioner who can meet the family where they want. They must have and children's rights training, shown in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Tell the family who it is, how to reach them and who the backup is. The family can ask for someone else. Enter both at FRM-ECS-04 question 3. Where the family later chooses a key worker from our team, that person becomes the plan lead (step 18).

Result
The family knows one named person of ours and the backup.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col D; FRM-ECS-04 Q3
Time limit
The day the family accepts our offer (our standard)
Step 2

The plan lead

Open the child's row in REG-ECS-01.

Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each have their own row, linked in column AF. Write the record number in column A. Write your name, role and the time in column D. Put the row number on FRM-ECS-02 question 1.

Result
The child has one record number that follows them through every early childhood record.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col A
Time limit
Within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard)
Step 3

The plan lead

Fill the family columns in REG-ECS-01 from what the family has already told us.

Use FRM-SUP-01 questions 7 and 8 and the documents the family gave at intake (REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register, when written, will hold intake and the service agreement). Enter the people in column E, the language and how the child communicates in column G, and who holds , on what basis and with any order reference, in column F. Write "not yet asked", with the date, for anything missing. Columns I and J are filled under PRO-ECS-02.

Result
The first session starts from what we know, and nobody asks the family the same question twice.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col E; REG-ECS-01 col F; REG-ECS-01 col G
Time limit
Before the first session (our standard)
Step 4

The plan lead

Explain to the family how we work.

Use the family's language and way. Say that the family leads and decides, and that we ask before we tell. Say the family can say no, skip any question and change their mind. Say a no never reduces a support. Say who their one contact is, and how to give feedback or complain. Offer pictures or an interpreter. Write what the family said back, in their words, at question 3.

Result
The family knows from the first session that they lead.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q3
Time limit
By the end of the first session (our standard)

Every contact with the family

Step 5

The practitioner

Read the family record before you see the family.

Read the priorities (question 19) and how they want information (question 9). Read the language and interpreter (question 24) and what they asked us to leave out (question 8). Read the beliefs and customs to respect (question 26). If the family record is not made yet, read REG-ECS-01 columns E and G and FRM-SUP-01 questions 7, 8 and 22. If you are covering for another practitioner, read the last contact record as well.

Result
You arrive knowing what matters to this family.
Record
None
Time limit
Before each contact (our standard)
Step 6

The practitioner

Ask the family what they want from today and what they have noticed since last time.

Ask before you tell. Let the family set the order. Ask what they have tried and what happened. A call or a message gets a shorter version of the same questions. Write what they said afterwards (step 13).

Result
The family's agenda leads, and their knowledge of their child comes first.
Record
None
Time limit
At the start of each contact (our standard)
Step 7

The practitioner

Work inside a routine the family has chosen.

Work where the routine happens: at home, at early learning or in the community. Use the child's own things, spaces and people. Do not add a separate therapy time unless the family chooses it. If a support must happen on our premises, the plan says why, the family has agreed and the Service Manager has signed it off (REG-ECS-01 columns M and AI).

Result
The strategy is practised where the child will use it.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)
Step 8

The practitioner

Explain what you see and why, in the way the family chose.

Use the language, format and amount the family chose at FRM-ECS-02 question 9. Use plain words and one idea at a time. Show what you mean with the child, a picture or a video, if the family likes. If you must use a technical word, explain it.

Result
The family has information they can use.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)
Step 9

The practitioner

Name one strength you saw.

Name a strength of the child, a parent, a carer, a brother or a sister. Say what they did. Tell the family it is worth building on. If you did not see one, ask the family what they saw.

Result
The family hears what is going well, and a strength is named at every contact.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)
Step 10

The practitioner

Ask the family to say or show you what they will try.

Do not ask "Do you understand?". Ask: "What will you do at bath time this week?", or ask them to show you. If the answer is unclear, say it another way. Ask the person who will do it.

Result
Any misunderstanding is found before you leave.
Record
None
Time limit
Before the end of each contact (our standard)
Step 11

The practitioner

Invite each family member to take part in the way they chose.

Check FRM-ECS-02 question 7. Let each person watch, try with your help, or lead. Do not take over a task a family member wants to do. Do not push a person who wants to watch. Invite brothers, sisters and other carers where the family wants it. Say what each person's part adds.

Result
Each person takes part as they chose, and their part is seen.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)
Step 12

The practitioner

Agree with the family what they will try before the next contact.

Agree one or two things, no more than the family says they have time and energy for (FRM-ECS-02 question 23). Link each one to a routine. Agree how the family will tell you how it went, and when you will next be in touch.

Result
The family has a small next step that fits their week.
Record
None
Time limit
Before the end of each contact (our standard)
Step 13

The practitioner

Write up the contact.

Use the session record, FRM-ECS-05 Session Record; a call or a message gets a short contact note on the same form. Write what the family asked for, said, chose and tried, and what they will try next, in their words where you can. Write the strength you named and how each person took part. Write any no, change request or difference of view, and follow step 21, 22 or 23.

Result
The record shows the family led the contact.
Record
FRM-ECS-05
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

The key worker

Step 14

The key worker, or the plan lead where the family chose no key worker

Agree with the family how you will keep in touch, and what you will and will not do.

Ask how often, by what method and at what times. Say what you will do: be the family's first call; deliver most of the coaching and strategies with the family yourself, drawing on the other team members' expertise, so the family works mainly with one person; bring the team's advice to them; and bring their priorities to the team. Say what you will not do: decide for the family, or speak for them unless they ask. Add this at FRM-ECS-04 question 19, in the family's words.

Result
The family knows who to call and what to expect.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q19
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the family's answer (our standard)
Step 15

The key worker, or the plan lead where the family chose no key worker

Start every team meeting with the family's priorities and what they want changed.

Ask the family beforehand what they want on the agenda, and whether they want to speak or be spoken for. Use FRM-ECS-02 question 19. Write the family's items first at FRM-ECS-04 question 23. Never speak for the family unless they ask.

Result
The team starts from what the family wants.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q23
Time limit
At every team meeting (our standard)
Step 16

The key worker, or the plan lead where the family chose no key worker

Give the family the team's advice as one plain message.

Put what each member advised into one message, in the family's language and format. Say where the advice differs and give the family the choice. Do not leave the family to work out what different services mean. Send notes only to members the family agreed to at FRM-ECS-04 question 7.

Result
The family has one clear message, and the choice is theirs.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q27
Time limit
Within 5 business days of each team meeting (our standard)
Step 17

The key worker, or the plan lead where the family chose no key worker

Ask the family whether the key worker arrangement still suits them.

Ask in the plan review conversation, together with PRO-ECS-03 step 28, so the family answers once. Ask whether it suits, and what they want to change. Where the family chose no key worker, ask whether they still want none. Ask the family, not the person beside them. The family can change it at any time (step 18). Record the next date to ask at FRM-ECS-04 question 20, and the answer in the one review record at FRM-ECS-02 question 38.

Result
The family has had the chance to change the arrangement.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q20; FRM-ECS-02 Q38
Time limit
At every plan review, and at least every 6 months (our standard)
Step 18

The plan lead

If the family wants a different key worker, or none:

Change the key worker as the family asks.

Say yes. Do not ask for a reason. Ask who they would like, and follow PRO-ECS-05 to find them. Add a dated line at FRM-ECS-04 question 17. If the new key worker is one of ours, they become the plan lead: update REG-ECS-01 column D and FRM-ECS-04 question 3 the same day and hand over the row. If the family chooses a key worker from another service, our plan lead stays and works to them (step 20). The outgoing key worker hands over only what the family agreed to share, so the family does not repeat their story. Supports carry on while the change happens.

Result
The family has the key worker they want, or none.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q17; REG-ECS-01 col D
Time limit
By the date the family chooses, or within 10 business days of the request (our standard)
Step 19

The Service Manager

If the key worker or the plan lead is away:

Put the backup in charge and tell the family.

The backup is named at FRM-ECS-04 question 3. Tell the family the backup's name and how to reach them. The backup reads the family record before the first contact. Add a new dated line at question 3. A planned change is told to the family at least 10 business days ahead.

Result
The family always has a named person of ours.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q3
Time limit
The same day for an unplanned absence. At least 10 business days ahead for a planned change (our standard)
Step 20

The plan lead

If the family's key worker is from another service:

Agree with the key worker how we will work with them.

Agree how we keep in touch and what we share, within the family's consent at FRM-ECS-04 question 7. Share the family record with them only as the family agreed. Our plan lead still keeps our family record and our row in REG-ECS-01, and works to the family's key worker.

Result
The family has one first call, and we work to it.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q18
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the family's choice (our standard)

When the family wants something different

Step 21

The practitioner

If the family says no to a question, a visit, a referral, a team meeting or part of a plan:

Record the no and carry on with everything else.

Say it is the family's choice. Write the date, what they said no to and what you will do instead at FRM-ECS-02 question 8. Ask again at the next plan review. Tell the plan lead the same day. Never reduce a support because of a no.

Result
The no is respected and on record, and no support is lost.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q8
Time limit
The same day (our standard)
Step 22

The plan lead

If the family asks to change times, place, practitioner or way of working:

Answer the request and make the change.

Tell the family whether the change can be made. If it can, make it by the date they ask. If it cannot, say why and offer the nearest option. Tell them in the way they chose. Write the request, the answer and the date done at FRM-ECS-02 question 8. If it changes the plan, change the plan with the family under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Result
The family's request has an answer, and the plan stays flexible.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q8
Time limit
Answer within 2 business days. Make the change by the date the family asks (our standard)
Step 23

The practitioner

If the family and a practitioner see something differently:

Record both views and agree the next step with the family.

Say what you see and why. Ask what the family sees. Do not argue or overrule. Write both at FRM-ECS-02 question 14. Agree what you will try and when you will look again. If the difference is about a child's safety, tell the child safety lead the same day and follow PRO-ECS-02.

Result
The family's view is on record and respected, and the next step is agreed.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q14
Time limit
The same day (our standard)
Step 24

Any worker

If the family is unhappy with a worker or with us:

Record it as a complaint and follow the complaints procedure.

Do not defend or explain first. Thank the family and say they will be heard. Record it on FRM-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Form and follow PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. The family can ask for a different practitioner while it is handled. A complaint never reduces a support.

Result
The family's complaint is handled under the complaints procedure.
Record
FRM-FBK-01
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Check the practice

Step 25

The plan lead. Where the plan lead wrote the records, another practitioner or the practice supervisor

Check the last three contact records against steps 5 to 13.

Read them at every plan review. Look for the family's agenda, a strength named, the family saying or showing what they will try, and each person taking part as they chose. Where the plan lead wrote the records, another practitioner or the reads them. Tell the practitioner what you find, and what went well, the same day. Write the gaps and what will change at FRM-ECS-02 question 43 (internal, not given to the family). A sole trader asks the practice supervisor to read their records, and the independent contact reads a sample.

Result
Gaps in the family-centred way of working are found and fixed, and are not left to chance.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q43
Time limit
At every plan review, and at least every 6 months (our standard)

6Decision

Decision table 1: when the family wants something different (steps 18 and 21 to 24).

IfThenStep
The family says no to a question, visit, referral, team meeting or part of a planRecord the no. Carry on with everything else. Ask again at the next plan review. Never reduce a support for a noStep 21
The family asks to change times, place, practitioner or way of workingAnswer within 2 business days. Make the change by the date they ask, or say why not and offer the nearest optionStep 22
The family and a practitioner see something differentlyRecord both views. Agree the next step with the family. Do not overrule themStep 23
The family wants a different key worker, or noneSay yes. Do not ask for a reason. Record it and hand overStep 18
The family is unhappy with a worker or with usTreat it as a complaintStep 24
Two people with parental responsibility want different thingsHear each person, unless an order or the family's recorded arrangement in REG-ECS-01 column F says one person decides about supports. Follow any order. Do not take sides. Record both views at FRM-ECS-02 question 5. Tell the Service Manager the same day. Supports continue as last agreedNone
A belief, custom or family practice may put the child at risk of harmDo not decide alone. Tell the child safety lead the same day. PRO-ECS-02 appliesNone
The family misses contacts or cannot be reachedContact them in the way they chose within 2 business days. Ask what would help. Offer another time, place or way. Missed contacts alone are not a reason to reduce or end supports. Any change follows PRO-SUP-01 Access to Supports Procedure, Decision table 3None

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A practitioner is absent for a contactThe Service Manager arranges cover the same day, using the arrangement the family agreed (REG-ECS-01 column Y). A practitioner the family knows is first choice. The cover practitioner reads the family record before the contact (step 5). Tell the family the same day
The family wants an interpreter and none is availableMove the contact, or use a phone or video interpreter. Never use a child or a brother or sister. Write what happened at step 13
The family cannot take part in the way they choseAsk what would help. Offer a different time, place or person. Do not treat it as lack of interest
A deadline in this procedure will be missedTell the Service Manager before the date. Tell the family why, and give the new date. The Service Manager sets a date within 10 business days, and the plan lead records the reason in REG-ECS-01
The plan lead is away for more than 5 business daysThe Service Manager names another worker to keep the row (step 19)
The row in REG-ECS-01 is not open by the first sessionThe session goes ahead. The plan lead opens the row the same day and records the reason for the delay. The only pre-session gate is the child's controls line in REG-ECS-01 column I (PRO-ECS-02 step 2)
Your concern is about a colleague or the managerTell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or the owner, tell the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, tell the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
A child may be at risk of harmTell the child safety lead the same day. PRO-ECS-02 applies. Do not investigate and do not promise to keep a secret
The system is downUse the paper form. Enter it in REG-ECS-01 within 1 business day of the system coming back

8Done means

Family-centred practice is in place for a family when all of these are true:

  • the family has a named plan lead and a backup, and a row in REG-ECS-01
  • the family has been told how we work, and what they said back is on record
  • each contact is written up the same day and shows the family led it
  • the family has the key worker they chose, or none, and knows who to call
  • every no, request for change, difference of view and complaint is on record and answered
  • the plan lead has checked the last three contact records at each plan review.

These records now exist:

  • the row in REG-ECS-01, with columns A, D, E and G filled
  • FRM-ECS-02 questions 3, 8 and 14
  • a session record (FRM-ECS-05) for every contact
  • FRM-ECS-02 question 43, after each plan review
  • the key worker entries in FRM-ECS-04, Section D
  • the complaint in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, if there was one.

9Quick card

110 words
  • Tell the child safety lead the same day if a child may be at risk of harm. PRO-ECS-02 applies (see Watch out and If it goes wrong)
  • Read the family record, then ask before you tell (step 6)
  • Work inside a routine the family chose (step 7)
  • Name one strength you saw (step 9)
  • Ask the family to say or show you what they will try (step 10)
  • Write up the contact the same day (step 13)
  • Open every team meeting with the family's priorities (step 15)
  • Record every no, and never reduce a support for it (step 21)
  • Answer a request for change within 2 business days (step 22)

10Control

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every has a team around them that the chose and can name. The team shares information, knowledge and skills only as the family agreed, and plans each move of the child with the family.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1 to C14.

2When and who

Start this procedure when a family accepts our offer of . Start again at step 21 each time you learn that a child will make a move. Steps 16 to 20 apply every day the child is with us.

Terms this procedure uses:

  • The is a completed FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record.
  • The is the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row. The plan lead also keeps the team record.
  • A is the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact and the main person who works with the family in their routines. Where the family chooses a key worker of ours, that person is the plan lead.
  • A is one row of the family's consent: one team member, one kind of information, one purpose.

Who acts:

  • The Service Manager opens the team record, names the backup and checks each record every 6 months.
  • The plan lead keeps the team record and does most steps with the family.
  • The key worker, when the family has one, may run team meetings with the plan lead.
  • Every practitioner of ours checks consent before sharing, and logs what they share.
  • The Quality Manager reviews the results once a year.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader names a backup at step 1, with the family's agreement: a locum engaged as our contractor, or a practitioner from another service under a written agreement with that service covering confidentiality, the NDIS Code of Conduct, worker screening evidence and the records the backup may see. A sole trader adds that person to the team at step 3 and gives them a consent line at step 5. For step 29 a sole trader checks their own records. For step 30 a sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns] to read a sample once a year.

3Before you start

  • The child's row is open in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register. PRO-ECS-01 Family-Centred Practice and Key Worker Procedure opens it.
  • You have the team record, on paper or in the system.
  • You have the family's communication preferences: FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • Section C of the team record (FRM-ECS-04 questions 6 to 12) is the family's consent record for sharing within the team.
  • You know how to book an interpreter: [interpreter service and how to book].
  • A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

4Watch out

  • A child at does not wait for consent. Go to step 18 at once. A delay can leave a child in danger.
  • Consent covers one person, one kind of information and one purpose. Sharing outside it breaches the family's privacy. It can also put them at risk, for example a family that has left a violent partner.
  • Only a person with can consent. A relative, a neighbour or an educator cannot. Decision table 1 says who can.
  • The family chooses the key worker. A key worker we steer them to takes away their choice and may serve us, not them.
  • Never use a child, a brother or a sister to interpret. It puts the child in the middle of an adult matter and can distort what is said.
  • Saying no must cost the family nothing. A family that declines a team, a key worker or a share keeps every support.

5Steps

Open the team record (Service Manager, plan lead)

Step 1

The Service Manager

Name our plan lead and backup to the family.

Copy the plan lead and the backup from REG-ECS-01 col D, which PRO-ECS-01 step 1 fills, into the team record at question 3, with the child's row number. The backup knows the child or can meet them. They can keep the record and take calls while the plan lead is away. Tell the family in the way they prefer, and give a way to reach each person. Do this step again each time the plan lead or the backup changes.

Result
The family knows who coordinates for us and who covers, and the child has one team record.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q1; FRM-ECS-04 Q3; REG-ECS-01 col D
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the family accepting our offer. For a change, at least 10 business days before a planned one and the same day after an unplanned one (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 4POL-ECS-05 C4Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 1FRM-ECS-04 Q1→FRM-ECS-04, question 3FRM-ECS-04 Q3

Step 2

The plan lead

Confirm who holds parental responsibility.

Ask the family who holds parental responsibility and on what basis: a parent, a court order, or a child protection agency's letter. Ask whether anything has changed, such as a new order, a separation or a move into care. Use Decision table 1. Ask to see any court order or agency letter. Write who holds it, on what basis, what the order or letter covers, its date and where the copy is filed. Question 2 of the team record holds the authority itself, and REG-ECS-01 col F points to it.

Result
You know who can consent for the child, and the family has seen that we checked.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q2; REG-ECS-01 col F
Time limit
At the first conversation with the family, before you ask for any consent (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 8POL-ECS-05 C8Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 2FRM-ECS-04 Q2

Step 3

The plan lead

Build the team with the family.

Ask who is in the child's life. Put the family first. Then add only the people the family names. Think of early learning, school, the doctor or child health nurse, therapists, other NDIS providers, and cultural or community supports. Write what each person does for the child and how to reach them. If the child has no other service yet, write "no other providers yet" and ask again at each review. Agree how the team keeps in touch between meetings. Settle the method, how often, who starts it and the longest a message may wait for an answer. That is up to 3 business days, or shorter if the family asks.

Result
The team is named in the family's words, and the family has agreed how it keeps in touch.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q4; FRM-ECS-04 Q5; REG-ECS-01 col P
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the plan lead being named (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 5POL-ECS-05 C5←POL-ECS-05, commitment 7POL-ECS-05 C7Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 4FRM-ECS-04 Q4→FRM-ECS-04, question 5FRM-ECS-04 Q5

Consent to share (plan lead)

Step 4

Warning. Consent given without understanding is not consent. A family that is rushed can agree to share more than they meant.

The plan lead

Explain consent and its limits to a person with parental responsibility.

Use the family's language and way of communicating. Book an interpreter if they want one. Say that they decide who is in the team. Say that they can say no to any person or item, and can change their mind on any day. Say that saying no costs no support. Say that the law may require us to share information without consent to keep a child safe, and that PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell them, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

Result
The person knows what they are agreeing to, and where the limits are.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q6
Time limit
Before anything is shared with any team member (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 10POL-ECS-05 C10Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 6FRM-ECS-04 Q6

Step 5

The plan lead

Record what the family agrees to share with each team member.

Go through the team one member at a time. For each, write the kinds of information we may give and may receive: assessment reports, the child's plan, progress notes, strategies, health information, family circumstances. Write the purpose and the method. Ask what must stay private, such as an address. Write who consented, their authority, the date and how, signed or spoken. If it was spoken, write the words used and who heard them. Set an end date: the end of the child's current plan period, or the end of the enrolment the consent is for, as the family chooses. Review every line at each plan review.

Result
Each consent line shows who may share what, with whom and why, and the family can read it.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q7; FRM-ECS-04 Q8; FRM-ECS-04 Q9; FRM-ECS-04 Q10; REG-ECS-01 col Q; REG-ECS-01 col E
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 4 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 8POL-ECS-05 C8Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 7FRM-ECS-04 Q7→FRM-ECS-04, question 8FRM-ECS-04 Q8→FRM-ECS-04, question 9FRM-ECS-04 Q9→FRM-ECS-04, question 10FRM-ECS-04 Q10and 1 more

Step 6

The plan lead

Give the family a copy of the team list and the consent lines.

Use a form the family can read: print, large print, audio, translated, or read through with an interpreter. Tell them whom to tell if they want to change anything.

Result
The family holds what they agreed and knows how to change it.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q11
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the consent being given (our standard)

Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 11FRM-ECS-04 Q11

The key worker (plan lead)

Step 7

The plan lead

Explain what a key worker is and ask whether the family wants one.

Say it in plain words. A key worker is the family's main contact and the main person who works with the family in their routines. They bring in the rest of the team and use its advice. PRO-ECS-01 sets how a key worker works through the family's routines. Use the family's language, and an interpreter if they want one. Write the date you asked and the answer. Use Decision table 2. Set the date to ask again.

Result
The family knows what a key worker is and has said yes, no or not yet.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q13; FRM-ECS-04 Q14; FRM-ECS-04 Q20; REG-ECS-01 col O
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the plan lead being named. Ask again at every plan review and at least every 6 months (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 1POL-ECS-05 C1Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 13FRM-ECS-04 Q13→FRM-ECS-04, question 14FRM-ECS-04 Q14→FRM-ECS-04, question 20FRM-ECS-04 Q20

Step 8

The plan lead

If the family wants a key worker:

Find possible key workers with the family and the other providers.

Start with what matters to the family: skills, language, culture, days and times, and someone the child already knows. Ask whom the family trusts. Then ask each provider in the team whether one of their people could take the role, as the consent lines in step 5 allow. Tell the family that the key worker may be ours or from another service in the team, and ask whom they trust. Record the options discussed. Say so if you or your service would gain from the choice. POL-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Policy applies.

Result
The family has real options, and the search is written down.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q15; FRM-ECS-04 Q16
Time limit
Start within 5 business days of the family saying they want one (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 2POL-ECS-05 C2Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 15FRM-ECS-04 Q15→FRM-ECS-04, question 16FRM-ECS-04 Q16

Step 9

The plan lead

If the family wants a key worker:

Help the family choose a key worker.

Give each option in plain words. The family may meet each person first. Do not push. The family chooses. If nobody can take the role, or the family wants to wait, write "not decided". Then name the plan lead as the family's main contact and set a date to look again within 20 business days. Use this step again when the family asks for a change or the key worker cannot continue.

Result
The family has chosen a key worker, or has chosen to wait with a date to look again.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q17; REG-ECS-01 col O
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the family saying they want one, or asking for a change (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 2POL-ECS-05 C2←POL-ECS-05, commitment 3POL-ECS-05 C3Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 17FRM-ECS-04 Q17

Step 10

The plan lead

Agree the role with the chosen person and their service.

Check the person is willing. Check their service agrees they have time for the role. Agree with the family and the key worker what the key worker will and will not do, and how often they will be in touch. Ask each other provider in the team whether they agree. Write each answer.

Result
The key worker, their service and the team members have agreed to the family's choice.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q18; FRM-ECS-04 Q19; REG-ECS-01 col O
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the family's choice (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 2POL-ECS-05 C2←POL-ECS-05, commitment 3POL-ECS-05 C3Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 18FRM-ECS-04 Q18→FRM-ECS-04, question 19FRM-ECS-04 Q19

Step 11

The plan lead

Tell the team who the key worker is.

Tell the family first, in the way they prefer. Then tell each team member the consent lines allow. Add the key worker's contact details to the team list. Add a line to the sharing log.

Result
Everyone in the team knows whom to go to.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q29
Time limit
Within 2 business days of step 10 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 2POL-ECS-05 C2Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 29FRM-ECS-04 Q29

Team meetings (plan lead)

Step 12

The plan lead

Book the team meeting with the family.

A key worker of ours may do this step with you. Offer times and places that suit the family, or a video or phone link. Ask what the family wants to talk about and whether the child will be there. Invite each team member the consent lines allow. Say who will interpret.

Result
The family chose the time and the way, and every member is invited.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q21; FRM-ECS-04 Q22
Time limit
Send invitations at least 10 business days ahead. Hold the first meeting within 20 business days of the child's plan being approved, or earlier if the family wants one. Where the child has no other provider yet, the plan review doubles as the team meeting (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 6POL-ECS-05 C6Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 21FRM-ECS-04 Q21→FRM-ECS-04, question 22FRM-ECS-04 Q22

Step 13

The plan lead

Run the meeting with the family's items first.

A key worker of ours may run it with you. Ask how the child shows what they like, fear and need, and include it. Each member says what they know and shows the strategies that work. Share only what the consent lines cover. Agree each action with one owner and one date. If members disagree, write each view. The family decides. Agree the next meeting date before you close.

Result
The family was heard first. The team has agreed actions, and the next date is set.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q23; FRM-ECS-04 Q24; FRM-ECS-04 Q25; FRM-ECS-04 Q26; FRM-ECS-04 Q28; REG-ECS-01 col R
Time limit
Set the next meeting no later than 6 months after this one (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 6POL-ECS-05 C6←POL-ECS-05, commitment 11POL-ECS-05 C11Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 23FRM-ECS-04 Q23→FRM-ECS-04, question 24FRM-ECS-04 Q24→FRM-ECS-04, question 25FRM-ECS-04 Q25→FRM-ECS-04, question 26FRM-ECS-04 Q26→FRM-ECS-04, question 28FRM-ECS-04 Q28and 2 more

Step 14

The plan lead

Send the notes to the family and the team.

Send the notes to the family first, in a form they can use. Send them to each member the consent lines allow, and only the parts that member may see. An absent member gets what they need to do their actions.

Result
The family and the team are in step.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q27; REG-ECS-01 col R
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the meeting (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 6POL-ECS-05 C6Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 27FRM-ECS-04 Q27

Step 15

The plan lead

Check each agreed action on its due date.

Ask the owner. If the action is not done, ask what is in the way and set a new date. Tell the family. If a member's service will not act, the family decides what happens next.

Result
Each action is done, or has a new date and the family knows.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q25
Time limit
On each due date (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 6POL-ECS-05 C6Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 25FRM-ECS-04 Q25

Sharing between meetings (every practitioner)

Step 16

Warning. Sharing outside the consent breaches the family's privacy. It can put a child or family at risk.

Every practitioner of ours

Share only what the family's consent covers.

Before each report, call, email, visit or strategy, read the consent lines in the team record, at questions 7, 8 and 12. Share if the person, the kind of information and the purpose are covered, and the line is not ended or withdrawn. If not, stop and ask the family first. Share nothing meanwhile. When you reply to a request, write the date it came in. Write child protection concerns nowhere in the team record. Add a line to the sharing log for every report or document sent or received, and for the first with any new person. For a routine call or email within an existing consent line, write "consent checked: Q7 line N" in the progress note instead. The Service Manager samples the notes at step 29.

Result
Only covered information was shared, and each exchange is in the sharing log or the progress note.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q29
Time limit
Check before each exchange. Log a document or a new recipient the same day (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 7POL-ECS-05 C7←POL-ECS-05, commitment 8POL-ECS-05 C8Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 29FRM-ECS-04 Q29

Step 17

Every practitioner of ours

Share knowledge and skills with the family and the team.

Show the family and each team member the strategies in the child's plan, in the child's own routine, and say why they work. Ask what they know of the child and use it. Note the strategy shown in the progress note, with the consent line used. Add a sharing log line when a document goes with it. For repeated sessions, use PRO-ECS-06 Capacity Building Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Result
The family and the team can use the strategies, and we have learned from them.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q29
Time limit
At every team meeting and every joint visit or call (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 11POL-ECS-05 C11Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 29FRM-ECS-04 Q29

Step 18

Warning. A child who is at risk can be harmed while you wait for consent or a meeting.

Any practitioner of ours

If you think a child may be at risk of harm:

Follow PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Do not wait for consent or for a meeting. Use FRM-ECS-01 Child Protection Concern and Report Record. The law of [state or territory] sets how fast you must report. PRO-ECS-02 says who tells the family and when.

Result
The concern is reported as the law of [state or territory] requires.
Record
FRM-ECS-01
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 10POL-ECS-05 C10Written on: →FRM-ECS-01FRM-ECS-01

Step 19

The plan lead

If a person with parental responsibility changes or withdraws consent:

Act on the change or withdrawal.

Stop the sharing the moment you are told. Write the date and time you were told and what changed. Tell each team member the change touches to stop sharing that item. Supports carry on. If the person who holds parental responsibility has changed, go back to step 2.

Result
Sharing has stopped, the consent lines are right, and the supports continue.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q12; REG-ECS-01 col Q
Time limit
The day you are told. Tell each team member within 1 business day (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-ECS-05, commitment 9POL-ECS-05 C9Written on: →FRM-ECS-04, question 12FRM-ECS-04 Q12

Step 20

The plan lead

Renew the consent.

Ask the family about 20 business days before the end date. Read each line with them. Ask whether any person, kind of information or purpose should change. If the family does not answer, ask a second way and tell the Service Manager. If the end date passes before the family has answered, you have 20 business days to confirm with them, and sharing under the line continues meanwhile. If there is still no answer after that, sharing stops and the supports continue.

Result
Each consent line is renewed with a new end date, changed, or ended.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q7; FRM-ECS-04 Q8; FRM-ECS-04 Q9; FRM-ECS-04 Q10; REG-ECS-01 col Q

Start planning the move with the family.

7If it goes wrong

  • You think a child is at risk of harm. Go to step 18 now. Tell the .
  • The parents disagree about sharing. Share only what both accept. Tell the Service Manager. Ask for any court order, and take legal advice if the Service Manager decides it is needed.
  • You shared something the family did not agree to, or received it. Stop. Tell the Service Manager the same day. The Service Manager follows PRO-INF-02 Privacy and Data Breach Response Procedure and tells the family.
  • You cannot reach the family for consent or renewal. Try 3 times by at least 2 different ways over 10 business days (our standard). Tell the Service Manager. Do not share until you have consent. The supports continue.
  • A provider will not join the team, or does not answer. Ask twice (our standard). Tell the family. The family decides whether to try another person at that service. The team goes on without them. Write what happened.
  • The key worker leaves, or the family wants a new one. Use step 9 and step 10 again. The plan lead is the family's main contact until a new key worker is in place, within 10 business days (our standard).
  • The plan lead is away. The backup acts and keeps the record. If both are away for more than 5 business days (our standard), the Service Manager names another worker and tells the family.
  • A deadline will be missed. Tell the family before the date and give a new date within 10 business days (our standard). Tell the Service Manager. The Service Manager writes the reason in the row in REG-ECS-01.
  • The team record is more than 6 months old. Do step 28 now (our standard). Tell the Service Manager.
  • The child's plan is overdue for review. Tell the Service Manager. Do step 28 now rather than wait. PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets the plan review.
  • The family does not want a team meeting. Offer another way to keep in touch, such as a call or notes shared through the key worker. Write the family's choice. Ask again at the next plan review.
  • No interpreter is available. Rebook. Do not use a child, a brother or a sister. Do not take consent until the interpreter can come. The supports continue.
  • You have a concern about a colleague. A concern about how a colleague practises goes to the . A concern about a colleague's conduct towards a child or family, or about safety, goes to the Chief Executive; a concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body or to [independent contact for concerns]. In a sole trader's business, tell [independent contact for concerns]. A concern that a worker has harmed a child follows PRO-ECS-02 and PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure the same day. This is the one rule POL-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Policy sets.
  • The family is unhappy with how we work as a team. Offer PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Saying so never costs them a support.

8Done means

  • The child has one team record with a named plan lead and backup, and the family knows them.
  • The team is named in the family's words, and REG-ECS-01 col P shows each member and what they do.
  • REG-ECS-01 col O shows the family's answer on a key worker, and the key worker if there is one.
  • Each consent line shows who may share what with whom, with an end date. REG-ECS-01 col Q matches.
  • Every team meeting is recorded, and REG-ECS-01 col R shows the next date.
  • Each document sent or received outside a meeting is in the sharing log, and each routine exchange names its consent line in the progress note.
  • Each move is named and dated, and REG-ECS-01 col AA shows planning, handover and confirmation.
  • The Service Manager has checked the record in the last 6 months.

9Quick card

132 words
  • A child may be at risk of harm: follow PRO-ECS-02 at once. Do not wait for consent. (step 18)
  • Check the consent lines before every exchange. If they do not cover it, ask the family first. (step 16)
  • Consent changed or withdrawn: stop sharing the day you are told. (step 19)
  • Confirm who holds parental responsibility before you ask for consent. (step 2)
  • Explain what a key worker is, and ask. The family chooses. (step 7)
  • Hold the first team meeting within 20 business days of plan approval, then at least every 6 months. (step 12)
  • Send the meeting notes within 5 business days. (step 14)
  • Learn of a move? Start planning within 10 business days. (step 21)
  • Hand over at least 10 business days before the child's first day. (step 24)

form.intro:
Use this record for every concern that a child is at , from anyone, in any place. It shows why we suspect, on reasonable grounds, that the child is at risk. It shows the report made to the child protection authority of [state or territory], and what happened next.

  • Section A: the practitioner who has the concern completes this the same day.
  • Section B: the child safety lead completes this during the worker's first call.
  • Section C: the person who made the report to the authority completes this. That is the worker, or the child safety lead.
  • Sections D and E: the child safety lead completes these as the concern is managed.

This record sits beside the incident report only where the harm is connected with the provision of our supports or with one of our workers (PRO-ECS-02 Decision table 2). In that case the worker's account of what happened goes on FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form, as for any incident, and question 4 here is a short reason only. Where the concern is not connected with our supports, there is no incident report and no NDIS Commission notice: question 4 carries the full account.

Phone the child safety lead before you start writing. If a child is in danger, call 000 first.

Have ready: the child's name, date of birth and address, and the names of the people who live with them. Have the reference number the authority gave you.

What happens next: the child safety lead gives this record a number and enters it in REG-ECS-01 col J. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. When systems are down, use the paper copy kept at [location at each site].
form.privacy:
We collect this information to keep a child safe and to make reports under child protection law. We also collect it to meet our duties under the NDIS Act 2013.

Only the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive read it. The Quality Manager and auditors read REG-INC-01 and REG-ECS-01 col J, not this form. The and the Service Manager receive only the outcome for the child's supports and plan (questions 14 and 18), by note. We give parts of it to the child protection authority, police, the NDIS Commission and other bodies. We do this when the law requires or allows it. A report to the authority needs no consent.

A person with parental responsibility can ask what we hold about their child. We may hold back parts if giving them could put the child at risk. We also hold back parts if the law or an authority tells us not to. We remove other people's details first. We never tell the person a concern is about who raised it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.

If it is about the Chief Executive or an owner, give it to the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, give it to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

form.intro:
This is the for one child. It names the and the key worker if the family chose one. It records what the family agreed may be shared, each team meeting and each planned move.

Keep one team record for each child. It stays open while we support the child. Add dated entries. Never write over an old entry.

Who completes it:

  • The Service Manager completes question 1, question 3 and question 41.
  • The plan lead completes the rest of Sections A to D, and Sections G and H, with the family.
  • The plan lead adds one entry to Section E for each team meeting. A key worker of ours may do it with them.
  • Every practitioner of ours adds a line to Section F each time they send or receive a document, or share with a new person.

Have these ready:

  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • nothing else for consent: Section C of this record is the family's consent record for sharing within the team
  • any court order or agency letter about who decides for the child
  • the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, once it is written.

PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The family receives a copy of Sections A to C, of questions 13 to 15 and 17 to 20, and of every meeting entry. Question 16 stays in the file.

Do not write a child protection concern in this record. Use FRM-ECS-01 Child Protection Concern and Report Record. If you do not know an answer, write "not yet asked" and the date. Ask at the next contact with the family.
form.privacy:
This statement is for the family.

We collect this information so the people who support your child can work as one team. The NDIS Practice Standards require us to coordinate that team and to share information only with your consent.

Our practitioners who work with your child read this record. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager.

We share your information with a team member only as you agree at question 7. You can say no to any person or any item. Your supports continue either way.

There is one exception. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can ask to see this record and ask us to correct it. You can change or withdraw your consent at any time by telling [contact person]. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Plan lead: give the family a copy of Sections A to C and of questions 13 to 15 and 17 to 20 within 5 business days of the consent at question 9 (our standard).
  • Plan lead: enter the key worker, the team, the consent dates and the meeting dates in REG-ECS-01. Do it within 2 business days of each change (our standard).
  • Plan lead: send each meeting entry to the family and the team within 5 business days of the meeting (our standard).
  • Plan lead: review the team record with the family at every plan review, and at least every 6 months (our standard).
  • Service Manager: answer question 41 for each child at least every 6 months (our standard).
  • Keep the team record in the child's file for 7 years after supports end (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026), or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard).
  • Check the law of [state or territory] before a child's record is destroyed. Some laws set a longer time.

register.proves:
This register holds one row for every who receives from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each plan, review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on inclusion, and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on practitioner skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention supports for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise version not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has .
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an interruption, a or an exit comes up. Columns AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AI, AJ, AK and AL are kept current for every row.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of setting it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final progress report and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.
